claim: Empowerment is the channel capacity from actions to later sensor states; in deterministic discrete worlds it equals log of the number of reachable states, so it measures how many distinct futures the agent can reliably cause.
agent_test: Definition only; count reachable outcomes for candidate probes.

claim: Empowerment becomes flat (uninformative) when the horizon is long or sensors are too rich; it needs a limited horizon or limited observability to rank states.
agent_test: Compare probe ranking by k-step vs unlimited lookahead at equal tokens.

claim: Empowerment alone does not pursue an external goal; a goal state with low empowerment is not sought. It is an exploration prior, not a goal-directed objective.
agent_test: Use empowerment-style probe choice only in open exploration; switch to goal value once a goal is set.
audit_note: Stated directly by Salge et al. (one source); Garg et al. only supports it indirectly (empowerment used as an auxiliary exploration bonus in goal-conditioned RL).

claim: Scalable empowerment estimators exist (variational bounds, latent-predictive, offline) and match exact values in small worlds, but gains over strong baselines are small and task-dependent.
agent_test: Not directly testable on a text scaffold; informs which estimators to avoid.

claim: In deep RL, empowerment bonuses give mixed exploration gains: in sparse-reward MiniGrid worlds an empowerment-inspired bonus beat the A2C baseline significantly in two of three environments (MultiRoom, KeyCorridor) but not in DoorKey-8x8, where only the curiosity agent was faster after outlier removal; the offline empowerment bonus beat CRL on 5 OGBench tasks and was on par elsewhere; best-of-N gains are small and task-dependent; and with PPO pretraining shows no clear improvement.
agent_test: Do not expect an empowerment term to beat plain info-gain probes; run both arms.
audit_note: Massari et al. found the empowerment-inspired agent significantly faster than the A2C baseline in MultiRoom-N3-S4 (p<0.001) and KeyCorridor-S3R1 (p=0.041); it was not significantly different only in DoorKey-8x8 (and the text describes three environments, not four).
claim_before_audit: In deep RL, empowerment bonuses give weak or mixed exploration gains: not significantly better than baseline when all runs are kept; helps on some offline tasks; small best-of-N gains; PPO shows no clear improvement.

claim: Information-gain (curiosity) bonuses help exploration in RL, but prediction-error variants are broken by self-generated noise (noisy TV).
agent_test: Prefer expected information gain over surprise or novelty when probes may return noisy answers.

claim: Learning a skill prior can collapse diversity (VIC 'Matthew effect'); a fixed uniform prior (DIAYN) kept many skills.
agent_test: Keep the hypothesis prior broad when sampling candidates; check for collapse of candidate diversity.

claim: Active inference expected free energy has a contested derivation: the epistemic term does not follow from free-energy minimisation, and the sign problem is real.
agent_test: Do not adopt EFE wholesale; use plain expected information gain.

claim: Active inference with information gain solved sparse-reward MountainCar in one trial and is comparable on some continuous-control tasks.
agent_test: None for a text agent.

claim: Choosing questions by explicit expected information gain computed by code over sampled hypotheses roughly doubles 20 Questions success versus prompting (BED-LLM: +37.4 pp on average per the paper, never decreasing across 6 LLMs; Table 1 means over the 18 cells are 70.7% vs 30.3% prompt-only, a 40.4 pp gap, with 11 of 18 cells more than doubling). Boundary from other tasks: on HumanEval clarifying questions the EIG gain is +14.8 pts for GPT-3.5 but +1.9 for GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-5 does not significantly benefit from Bayesian question selection in Battleship.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare LLM-judged best probe vs EIG-scored probe over sampled hypotheses in S7.
audit_note: The paper's abstract says +37.4 pp, but the Table 1 means (70.7 vs 30.3) differ by 40.4 pp, so the claim's two figures contradict each other; also the 'GPT-4o-mini vs GPT-3.5' boundary comes from HumanEval/APPS clarifying questions (Kobalczyk et al.), not from 20 Questions, and BED-LLM's own gains do not shrink for stronger models (GPT-4o 45 to 93 on Animals).
claim_before_audit: Choosing questions by explicit expected information gain computed by code over sampled hypotheses roughly doubles 20 Questions success versus prompting (BED-LLM +37.4 percentage points, never decreasing across 6 LLMs). Boundary: gains shrink for strong models (GPT-4o-mini vs GPT-3.5 in 20Q; GPT-5 in Battleship). Mean over 18 BED-LLM cells: 70.7% vs 30.3% prompt-only.

claim: UoT reports +38.1% average success over direct prompting across 5 datasets and 5 LLMs. Recomputing Table 1 shows the 46.6% Llama3-70B figure is a mean of per-cell RELATIVE gains (absolute gain about 10 points), so 38.1% is relative and must not be compared with BED-LLM's +37.4 percentage points. At matched tokens (about 4.6k, GPT-4, closed set) pruned UoT beat CoT-SC over questions (k=33): 48.1/88.4/63.2 vs 32.6/37.6/42.5 on 20Q/diagnosis/troubleshooting.
agent_test: Compare an EIG tree with self-consistency on the FINAL answer at equal tokens on open reasoning items; the published matched-budget test only voted on questions.

claim: Asking the LLM to judge or imagine the most informative question (implicit maximisation, raw in-context beliefs, CoT) is much worse than explicit EIG scoring; raw in-context belief updates are incoherent and overconfident.
agent_test: Do not let the model self-rate probe informativeness; score by partition of sampled hypotheses.

claim: Predictive entropy equals EIG only when answers are deterministic given the hypothesis. With noisy answers, entropy-only scoring was worse than full EIG in 18 of 18 BED-LLM cells (mean 57.6 vs 70.7) and gave no gain over prompting in preference elicitation; full EIG needs no extra calls. If the noise rate is the same for all probes (binary symmetric channel), entropy and EIG rank probes identically (derivation from Shoot First, eq. 4); they diverge only when noise differs by probe.
agent_test: Do not use the entropy proxy when probes have different noise (code that may crash, tool output of varying reliability); use full EIG or estimate a per-probe noise rate.
audit_note: The BSC rank-equivalence is the claim's own derivation (it follows from eq. 4 since EIG is monotone in |p-0.5|), not a statement in the paper.

claim: The EIG advantage shrinks when the target is a soft profile rather than a concrete entity, and weighting by model log-probabilities hurts (EIG-uniform beat EIG-logprobs).
agent_test: Measure probe benefit separately for closed-set and open-ended tasks.
audit_note: BED-LLM only says Prompt-Only is a stronger baseline on the film task and BED-LLM still helps; 'shrinks' is an inference with no per-turn numbers; OPEN (c18) does not address it.

claim: Frontier LLMs reduce uncertainty each turn but ask more questions than an exact planner; many LMs ask low-value questions humans do not; unaided GPT-4 finds about one third of 20 Questions entities.
agent_test: Measure probes-to-resolution against an oracle EIG planner.
audit_note: 'Many LMs' rests on two named models (Llama-4-Scout 18.5%, GPT-4o 14.6% redundant questions); GPT-4 about 1/3 is from Zhang et al. 2024.

claim: Monte Carlo EIG strategies lift weak LMs above humans and frontier models on Collaborative Battleship at a fraction of cost (Llama-4-Scout F1 0.367 to 0.764; 0.67 win rate vs GPT-5 at 1% of cost). GPT-5 itself did not significantly benefit from Bayes question or move selection, and the question step alone added only +0.021 to +0.026 F1 for Scout and GPT-4o; the large jump needs the move and decision modules.
agent_test: Pair a small model plus EIG selector against a larger unscaffolded model at equal cost.

claim: Training can internalise EIG-based questioning (DPO on EIG-labelled pairs raises Llama-2-7B success from 56.7 to 68.9 on INLG; RL with an EIG reward more than doubles 7B success on 20 Questions), but the benefit shrinks at larger scale: the 14B model improves by only +4.2 (animals) and +1.8 (plants) points.
agent_test: Out of scope (no training); a scaffold can supply the EIG computation instead.
audit_note: ASIG is trained separately at each size; the paper reports a smaller gain at 14B (+4.2 animals, +1.8 plants points vs more than doubling at 7B) and says it transfers well to MediQ at 7B, so 'transfer across model size is weak' misstates it.
claim_before_audit: Training can internalise EIG-based questioning (DPO on EIG-labelled pairs; RL with EIG reward), but transfer across model size is weak (14B gains +4.2 and +1.8 points).

claim: LLMs under-use empowerment as an exploration signal: in Little Alchemy 2 only o1 (177 elements) and R1 (85) beat humans (42); most models weight uncertainty, not empowerment; prompting and steering did not fix it. The prompt test used verbal hints on GPT-4o only (43 elements vs 35 baseline, p=0.304); a computed per-candidate option count has not been tested.
agent_test: Add an explicit option-count hint to probe choice and compare with uncertainty-only at equal tokens.

claim: Empowerment of an LM agent estimated from text trajectories tracks performance: removing CoT drops it 99% (Gridworld) and 65% (Hanoi); WebArena Spearman 0.83-0.94 in three domains but flat in Shopping, and it breaks when agents wander off task. It beats simple trace statistics only as an aggregate across models: WebArena Spearman 0.39 vs 0.16 best baseline (N=16), tau-bench 0.71 (N=6) but inverts on tau-bench retail at floor performance.
agent_test: Use as a monitor of whether a reasoning trace opens future options; validate on our own traces.

claim: Maximising human empowerment as an assistant objective helps: simulated-human Pass@1 more than doubles (192% average gain over SFT); an 18-person study preferred it 78% (p=0.015).
agent_test: Little relevance to a solo reasoning agent; design analogy only.

claim: Humans prefer controllable and variable machines when producing new outcomes; in free play, entropy and empowerment correlate with progress. The goal-statement result (r=0.8, p=0.005 unadjusted) rests on 10 children with at least 5 utterances (17 children had transcripts, 26 children analysed, 51 recruited), with goals labelled by gpt-3.5-turbo; it is not replicated. In ELLM (Crafter RL), goal conditioning of the policy gave no significant advantage.
agent_test: Test a goal-stating step before exploratory probes; small-n, treat as hypothesis.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs explore poorly in bandits: only one configuration (GPT-4 with explore hint and externally summarised history) explored well; basic GPT-4 shows suffix failure in over 60% of replicates; GPT-3 shows no directed exploration in the horizon task.
agent_test: Provide externally computed summaries (counts, per-option averages) during probe selection.

claim: Clarifying questions chosen by information gain over sampled solutions improve code and medical-diagnosis tasks (CuriosiTree, active task disambiguation), but gains depend on model and task and come from small setups.
agent_test: Try EIG-selected clarifying probes on our hardest ambiguous items.
audit_note: c14 and b16 are the same paper (Kobalczyk et al.), but CuriosiTree and the preference-inference paper are independent.

claim: Intrinsic exploration rewards during RL of reasoning LLMs improve GRPO on AIME 2024 by up to 22.23% relative at about 20% more training time.
agent_test: Training only; no scaffold test.

claim: Position papers argue LLMs fit active inference (missing an action-perception loop) or should use free energy in place of reward; none gives benchmark data.
agent_test: Treat as unsupported until measured.

claim: A moderate hypothesis set is enough to choose a probe: in BED-LLM the ranking of 5 candidate questions at 10 sampled hypotheses matched the ranking at 85 (one game); default settings across papers are N=15 to 20 hypotheses and M=5 to 15 candidates; best-of-M question scoring keeps raising EIG up to about M=10 and reaches 94.2% of the ceiling in Battleship. Diversity of hypotheses matters as much as count (MI score 0.57 vs 0.46 at N=10).
agent_test: Sample about 10 to 15 diverse hypotheses and 5 to 10 candidate probes; test argmax stability against a larger sample on 20 of our own items. Cost is N + M + N x M scored calls unless an executor answers.

claim: Failures of probe choice start with the hypothesis set, not the scoring: unfiltered in-context beliefs drop EIG below plain prompting (26.8 vs 30.3 mean over 18 cells), 200 independent samples collapse onto a few names, and LLMs in multi-turn settings answer early and rely on earlier wrong attempts (aptitude -15%, unreliability +112%).
agent_test: Add a consistency filter (every hypothesis must agree with every observation) before scoring; restate the live hypothesis set at each probe step. Test by ablating the filter.
audit_note: Table 1 means recomputed from the 18 cells: ICL Beliefs 26.8, Prompt-Only 30.3.

claim: With an execution oracle the answer noise is near zero and EIG-selected clarifying tests raise code accuracy (HumanEval after 4 questions: Llama3-8B 53.0 to 65.8, GPT-3.5 70.8 to 85.6, GPT-4o-mini 79.6 to 81.5), but the gain is smaller for stronger models and was never compared with a token-matched baseline.
agent_test: Probe by running candidate programs on a sampled input; score by how the sampled programs' outputs split. Compare with sampling the same number of extra programs and voting.

claim: EIG-weighted probe choice has no tested stopping rule in the LLM literature beyond a confidence threshold plus a cost budget (CuriosiTree: stop when the top class probability passes tau, cost weight lambda=0.1, 50 trials, one diagnosis). Theory gives (1-1/e) and ln-type greedy guarantees for noiseless adaptive submodular objectives only.
agent_test: Stop probing when best EIG per token falls below the expected value of one more reasoning step, or when the leading hypothesis passes a set probability. Calibrate the threshold on held-out items.

claim: EELMA-style empowerment is not a ready cheap monitor: it correlates with performance only across model-domain aggregates (N=16 and N=6), needs a trained estimator, and inverts when weak models produce diverse invalid outputs. No per-trace failure prediction (AUC) was found.
agent_test: Compare cheap trace statistics (repeat rate, distinct valid outcomes) against an empowerment estimate for per-run failure prediction on our own traces.
